source.title: The Geometry of Concepts: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Structure
source.authors: Yuxiao Li; Eric J. Michaud; David D. Baek; Joshua Engels; Xiaoqing Sun; Max Tegmark

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures geometric structure in SAE features and discusses possible refinements to theories of superposition, but it does not test the listed claims about toy-model superposition, capacity pressure, polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery, canonical feature units, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The paper analyzes SAE feature geometry in Gemma-2-2b; it does not test whether sparse features compete for dimensions or are stored in superposition. The toy-model superposition work is cited as background. Rows record the paper's own geometric findings, which do not measure a listed version.
record.test_reason: The paper measures the geometry of SAE decoder vectors in Gemma-2-2b: crystals, co-occurrence lobes, and the eigenvalue spectrum and clustering of the point cloud. No result bears on whether a listed version holds. It has no toy networks (V1), no capacity or polysemanticity test (V2, V3), and no test of distributed coding or SAE recovery (V4). It does not test SAE completeness, stability or canonicity (V5); it only raises the question. It also has no 1-D versus multi-D test (V6). The toy-model superposition work and linear-representation assumptions are background only.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. SAE features show structure at three scales: crystals revealed after removing distractors, spatially modular functional lobes, and an anisotropic power-law point cloud steepest in the middle layers. The authors do not explain the origin and suggest it may refine superposition theory.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes SAE-feature geometry in Gemma-2-2b and does not reproduce the original toy-network method or its measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The co-occurrence affinity measure affects the lobe results; the phi coefficient gives the best correspondence. The eigenvalue-spectrum slope and clustering entropy vary by layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Initial SAE crystal search found mostly noise. In early-layer activations, LDA projection of distractor directions (e.g., word length) dramatically improved parallelogram/trapezoid and cluster quality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantically irrelevant distractor directions obscure analogy-like crystal structure; projecting them out reveals it.

fits_no_version.finding: In the Layer 12 SAE (16k features), co-occurrence lobes match geometric clusters far beyond chance: AMI 954 sigma and logistic-regression accuracy 74 sigma above null. The phi coefficient gives the best match.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functionally co-occurring SAE features cluster spatially. This contrasts with the near-orthogonal spread expected from toy superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-feature covariance spectra follow power laws, steepest in the middle layers: slope -0.47 at L12 versus -0.24 at L0 and -0.25 at L24. They decay more steeply than activation spectra.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The SAE feature point cloud is anisotropic, with layer-dependent power-law eigenvalue decay.

fits_no_version.finding: Clustering entropy (negentropy) is highest in the middle layers. In one Gemma Scope SAE, low-frequency features dip toward earlier PCA components.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How strongly the SAE feature point cloud clusters, and where features sit in the PCA basis, depends on layer and feature frequency.

record.problems: The main analyses use Gemma-2-2b and a particular Layer 12 SAE for the lobe study. Several comparisons are described qualitatively or shown in figures without exact values in the text. The study does not test the origin of the observed feature geometry.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, sparsity sweep, phase transition, or regular geometry. The LLM SAE features cluster rather than spread apart, but that is not the toy setting.
All of it: no test of capacity competition or importance-driven dedicated dimensions.
All of it: neurons and polysemanticity are not studied.
Whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAEs recover the model's true features; the paper assumes SAE features are concepts.
Completeness, stability and canonicity are not tested. The authors only ask whether single SAE features are the natural unit of analysis.
Features are assumed to be 1-D directions; multi-dimensional features are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: R1 state corrected to absent. Unrecorded results also bear on no version: Figure A1 (phi coefficient vs cosine-neighbour rank, weaker at L0), Figure 8 log-determinant by layer, and Figure A3 LDA silhouette scores. The paper is a possible context source for whether SAE feature geometry departs from toy-model near-orthogonality, but it makes no toy-model comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, excess sparse features, overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The study analyzes SAE features in an LLM, but does not test feature distribution across neurons or whether an SAE recovers the model's features.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features are not tested.
The paper treats SAE decoder vectors as directions but does not test whether underlying model features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Searched SAE feature point cloud for crystal structure
rows.measure: Qualitative presence of parallelogram or trapezoid crystal structure
rows.note: The authors then focus on model activations in an early layer to investigate why the SAE crystal search was noisy.
rows.check: Text says the initial SAE crystal search 'found mostly noise', i.e., no structure detected. That is absent, not partial. Layer is not stated.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Compared candidate crystal geometry before and after projecting out distractor directions with LDA
rows.baseline: Candidate quadruplets before projecting out distractors
rows.value: LDA dramatically improves cluster and parallelogram/trapezoid quality
rows.note: The paper describes distractor directions, including a Layer 0 component associated mainly with word length.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Compared geometry-based feature clusters with clusters based on co-occurrence affinity

conditions.value: 50k documents from The Pile; co-occurrence counted within 256-token blocks

rows.measure: Adjusted mutual information between spatial and functional clusters
rows.baseline: Adjusted mutual information with randomly permuted cosine-similarity-based cluster labels
rows.value: Phi-based clustering rules out the null hypothesis at 954 standard deviations
rows.uncertainty: 954 standard deviations reported as significance; other uncertainty not stated
rows.note: The authors report that the phi coefficient gives the best correspondence between functional lobes and feature geometry.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Predicted co-occurrence-based lobe labels from feature positions using logistic regression
rows.measure: Balanced test accuracy for predicting functional lobe from geometry
rows.value: True feature directions rule out the null hypothesis at 74 standard deviations
rows.uncertainty: 74 standard deviations reported as significance; exact accuracy and other uncertainty not stated
rows.note: The paper reports the significance level but not the exact balanced test accuracy in the text.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Compared covariance eigenvalue spectra for SAE features and neural activations
rows.value: SAE features show a significantly steeper power-law decay; activations show much slower decay and weaker power-law behavior
rows.note: No numerical slope for the activation comparison is given in the text.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Estimated clustering entropy of the SAE feature point cloud across layers

conditions.value: across layers; individual layer values not stated in text

rows.measure: Clustering entropy, defined as Gaussian entropy minus estimated entropy
rows.baseline: Gaussian entropy for the same covariance matrix
rows.value: The SAE point cloud is described as strongly clustered, particularly in middle layers; the figure shows 95% confidence intervals
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals shown; exact values not stated
rows.note: The authors also describe clustering entropy as reduced at intermediate layers.

rows.subject: Gemma Scope 2b SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured the PCA score of SAE decoder vectors, then smoothed by feature-frequency rank
rows.measure: Weighted PCA score across SAE features
rows.value: An intriguing dip into earlier PCA features appears in the last third of SAE features
rows.note: The authors state that similar results appear on all Gemma Scope SAEs, but display one SAE.
rows.check: Subject is an SAE trained on Gemma-2-2b, not a model itself. 'Intriguing dip' is qualitative, read from Figure A4.
